newsitem.title: FRANCE: CIC denies capital injection warning.
newsitem.headline: CIC denies capital injection warning.

text.p: French bank group Credit Industriel et Commercial on Thursday denied having said it would need a capital injection of three or four billion francs if it was not privatised.

Les Echos newspaper quoted union sources as saying CIC boss Philippe Pontet told them the regional bank group could need a capital increase of three to four billion francs if plans by the previous government to privatise it were not enacted soon.
"It's a flat denial. They certainly did not receive such information," a CIC spokeswoman said in reply to a Reuter query.

"He (Pontet) said this is a state-controlled group and it's up to the state to decide," she said. "We will now have to see who will be the people (in the new Sociialist government) who will deal with this," she said.
The former centre-right government planned to privatise CIC this year after abandoning an initial tender to privatise it by trade sale late last year.
It also planned to privatise CIC's parent, state-controlled insurer GAN.
